newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian state backs car-makers with ad campaign.
newsitem.headline: Australian state backs car-makers with ad campaign.

text.p: Australia's Victoria state government on Thursday announced it would back local car makers with a major advertising campaign arguing against proposed cuts to tariffs on imported cars.

Victoria Industry Minister Mark Birrell said Australia's car-making industry would be devastated if the national government accepted an advisory body's proposal to slash import tariffs to five percent by year 2004.
About 60 percent of Australia's A$7.5 billion car-making industry is based in Victoria. It employs 45,000 people.
Victoria's ad campaign will be run nationally and argue for a freeze on tariffs at 15 percent until at least 2005, Birrell said in a statement.
Tariffs are already scheduled to fall to 15 percent in year 2000 from 22.5 percent now, but Australia's Productivity Commission has suggested tariffs be cut to five percent by 2004.
The commission has presented its final advice to the government on tariffs, but Canberra has yet to release it.
Australia has four car makers, all foreign owned. They are General Motors Holden, a unit of General Motors Corp, Ford Motor Co, Toyota Motor Corp, and Mitsubishi Motors Corp.
